text:
Alexandre Texier has gone nine straight games without a point, and the chances say that is mostly luck. Over that stretch he generated 3.5 expected goals' worth of looks for himself (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and Montreal's coaches have kept trusting him: his ice time rose to 17 minutes in his last two games.

On the season he has 5 points (2 goals) in 23 games, two goals on 4.65 expected and a shooting percentage of 4.9, far below his usual range. The Canadiens have also scored 4.97 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, while dominating play: 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with Texier out there.

There was a scare this week. RotoWire and Dose.ca reported he missed practice on Tuesday, and Montreal Hockey Fanatics framed it as "another concern" for Martin St. Louis, but he played the next two games. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season against tough competition, so this isn't a hidden star. It is a useful middle-six forward whose results have lagged his process. We'd watch whether the bigger minutes stick.
